headline: Quiet overnight: futures lower after Tesla, bitcoin holds near $82,800
summary: Stocks closed higher Wednesday (Nasdaq +1.05%, S&P 500 +0.58%, TSX +0.60%), but U.S. futures have since turned lower: S&P 500 futures were down about 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 0.7% around 9 p.m. ET after Tesla erased an early after-hours gain and Meta's jump faded to about 2%. Bitcoin is holding near $82,800, roughly flat on the day and about 2% below this evening's high near $84,700, while total crypto market value is down about 2.7% in 24 hours to roughly $2.79 trillion as crypto tracks weaker tech futures. Brent near $110 and a 10-year yield above 5.1% remain the main headwinds ahead of next week's Fed and Bank of Canada decisions.

crypto.label: Cautious
crypto.why: The Fear & Greed index reads 68 (Greed), but bitcoin gave back most of Wednesday's bounce within hours, is still down about 3% over 30 days, and ether ETFs keep losing money.

stocks.label: Cautious
stocks.why: Wednesday's close was strong and the VIX sits near 16.7, but futures turned lower after Tesla's reversal while a 10-year yield above 5.1% and Brent near $110 cap valuations.

drivers.title: Big Tech earnings: Meta up, Tesla reverses
drivers.detail: Meta beat on revenue and was still up a little over 2% after hours, while Tesla flipped from an early gain to a loss of more than 3% as investors focused on falling operating income and Musk's slower-than-hoped timeline for its Optimus robot. That reversal pulled S&P 500 futures down about 0.4% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 0.7% by about 9 p.m. ET; Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon report next week.

drivers.title: Stablecoin rules finalized
drivers.detail: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), a top U.S. bank regulator, finalized reserve, redemption and risk rules for stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, taking effect in January 2027. Circle rose about 6%, Coinbase about 4–5% and Strategy about 8%, though whether exchanges can keep paying stablecoin 'rewards' is still unsettled.

drivers.title: High yields and a Fed on hold
drivers.detail: The 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to about 5.15% after September CPI ran hot at 3.7%. Futures price a high chance the Fed holds at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28, but CME data cited by Nexo shows roughly 75% odds of a hike later this year.

drivers.title: Brent back above $110
drivers.detail: Brent traded above $110 a barrel in Asian trading after a drone attack on a Saudi Aramco oil field and continued tanker attacks around the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. price on the dashboard (December contract) is up about 1.2% to about $98.30.

drivers.title: Crypto ETF flows split
drivers.detail: Spot bitcoin ETFs took in about $550 million over Monday and Tuesday, but on-chain tracker Lookonchain estimated small outflows on Wednesday (about $34 million for bitcoin and $31 million for ether funds). Ether funds have lost about $1.08 billion this month, so money still favours bitcoin over ether.

drivers.title: Bank of Canada expected to hold
drivers.detail: Canadian headline inflation rose to 3.1% on gas prices, but core measures eased. Economists expect the Bank to hold at 2.25% on Oct. 28, which supported bank stocks today.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Flat (+0.1%) in 24h and up 1.5% this week, to about $82,800 (down about 3.2% over 30 days); down about 0.8% in the last hour
crypto.why: Bitcoin hit a one-week high near $84,700 on Wednesday as tech stocks rallied and short sellers were forced to buy back (liquidations, when leveraged bets get closed automatically; about $208 million of short bets were wiped out in 24 hours, per CoinGlass). It then slid back below $83,000 in the evening as U.S. stock futures turned lower after Tesla's results, showing it is still trading closely with the Nasdaq. Spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin) took in about $550 million on Monday and Tuesday, but early estimates point to a small outflow on Wednesday.
crypto.meaning: The quick give-back shows buyers aren't yet strong enough to push it out of the $80,000–$87,000 range it has held for a month. An on-chain analyst at CryptoQuant warns that weakness in both bitcoin and the S&P 500 at once has preceded deeper drops before, though that is one view, not a forecast.

outlook.bullCase: Reclaiming $84,000–$84,700 with steady ETF inflows and a firmer Nasdaq could carry it to the top of the range near $87,000–$87,500; a break above that would be a bigger shift.
outlook.bearCase: Weak tech trading Thursday, a hawkish Fed on Oct. 28, or higher yields and oil could push it to the $82,400 support and then the $80,000 floor.
outlook.watch: Thursday's Nasdaq open, Wednesday's official ETF flow figures, the 10-year yield near 5.15%, and the Fed decision on Oct. 28.

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Down 0.3% in 24h, up 1.1% this week, to about $2,437 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Ether briefly rose to about $2,490 with bitcoin on Wednesday, then gave the gain back in the evening, and it keeps trailing as U.S. ether ETFs kept losing money: about $26 million on Tuesday and an estimated $31 million more on Wednesday, taking October outflows past $1 billion, the worst month of 2026. On the plus side, a record 43.8 million ETH (about 36% of supply) is staked, meaning locked up to secure the network, though the average staking yield slipped to 2.63%.
crypto.meaning: Ether is lagging bitcoin because big investors keep pulling money from the ETFs. Until those flows turn, rallies may be harder to sustain.

outlook.bullCase: ETF outflows stopping and a firm hold above $2,500 could open a move toward about $2,700, where October began.
outlook.bearCase: Continued outflows or a broad risk-off turn could send it back below $2,400 toward the $2,300 area; it is already testing that zone.
outlook.watch: Daily ether ETF flows, the $2,400 and $2,500 levels, and the ETH/BTC ratio.

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Up 2.5% in 24h and 15% this week, to about $1,293 (still down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders are positioning for the NU7 upgrade, which developers scheduled for about 7:50 p.m. ET on Nov. 5; it cuts block times from 75 to 25 seconds and sends 60% of fees to a reserve. Futures open interest (the value of open bets) rose about 19–24%, and two large traders reportedly opened about $37.6 million of 10x leveraged longs. Bitwise's Zcash ETF saw small inflows Tuesday after outflows the day before.
crypto.meaning: Much of this rally is driven by leverage, and data show sellers stayed active during the rise, so swings both ways can be sharp. Upgrade dates often bring 'buy the rumour, sell the news' behaviour.

outlook.bullCase: Clearing resistance near $1,375 could bring the September high around $1,700 into view as the upgrade nears.
outlook.bearCase: Leveraged longs getting flushed could pull it back to the $1,190–$1,230 support area, and losing $1,180 would erase the breakout.
outlook.watch: $1,375 resistance, funding rates and open interest, ETF flows, and any upgrade delay.

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Up 11.2% in 24h and 22% this week, to about $3.76 (still down about 20% over 30 days)
crypto.why: The token of the Lighter derivatives exchange jumped after reports from its Oct. 21 investor call that it plans to apply for a U.S. licence in November and is weighing access through Robinhood's U.S. platform; neither has been confirmed. Renewed attention on its existing Robinhood Wallet partnership and a Delphi Digital research report added interest.
crypto.meaning: The move rests on unconfirmed plans. Only 25% of the 1 billion tokens are circulating, so future supply is a long-term overhang, and the token is still about half its all-time high.

outlook.bullCase: An official licence filing or Robinhood announcement could push it toward the $4.50–$5 area.
outlook.bearCase: No confirmation, or profit-taking after a 20% day, could send it back toward $3.20, the bottom of today's range.
outlook.watch: Official statements from Lighter, trading volume versus Hyperliquid, and token unlock schedules.

crypto.name: NEAR Protocol
crypto.move: Up 2.0% in 24h, 8.5% this week and 18% over 30 days, to about $5.13
crypto.why: NEAR has been one of October's strongest large coins. Supports include the first U.S. spot NEAR ETF from Bitwise (launched Sept. 29), a governance proposal to cut yearly new-token issuance from 2.5% to 1.6%, and strong use of its NEAR Intents cross-chain swap service. It was the top performer in the CoinDesk 100 today, without a single fresh headline.
crypto.meaning: The rally has real drivers behind it, but the issuance cut is only a proposal and NEAR is already back near its early-October highs around $6. Fast multi-week runs tend to see sharp pullbacks.

outlook.bullCase: Approval of the issuance cut and continued ETF inflows could push NEAR back to test the $5.60–$6.00 area hit earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If momentum fades or the proposal stalls, a pullback toward roughly $4.50–$5.00 would be typical after a run this size.
outlook.watch: The issuance-cut vote, NEAR ETF flows, and whether $5 holds.

crypto.name: Ethena
crypto.move: Up 4.6% in 24h and 7.6% this week, to about $0.207
crypto.why: ENA led large-cap gainers, but coverage today points to technical momentum rather than a single news event; the hourly RSI, a gauge of how overstretched a move is, hit about 73, which is considered overbought. A longer-term support is that the last tranche of early-investor tokens unlocked on Oct. 5, ending Ethena's monthly investor unlocks after the foundation bought out many early backers in August.
crypto.meaning: With the investor unlock overhang gone, ENA's supply picture is cleaner, but USDe, the synthetic dollar that drives Ethena's revenue, is far below its 2025 peak. A one-day pop on no clear news can unwind just as fast.

outlook.bullCase: A sustained move above about $0.2165, with USDe supply growing again, could carry ENA toward the mid-$0.20s.
outlook.bearCase: If the overbought bounce fades, a drop under about $0.195 (its 50-day average) would erase this week's gains.
outlook.watch: USDe supply, the $0.195–$0.2165 range, and broader altcoin risk appetite.

crypto.name: XRP
crypto.move: Up 1.0% in 24h and 1.7% this week, to about $1.34 (down 11% over 30 days)
crypto.why: XRP was the strongest of the major coins today in a broad altcoin bounce. Ripple's push to offer round-the-clock stock trading on crypto rails is in the news, though no single XRP-specific catalyst explains the gain.
crypto.meaning: XRP tends to move more than bitcoin in both directions, so today's outperformance mostly reflects higher risk appetite. The 30-day trend is still down.

outlook.bullCase: A broader crypto rally led by bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 could lift XRP back toward the $1.45–$1.50 area.
outlook.bearCase: If bitcoin slips back under $82,500, XRP would likely give back today's gains and retest about $1.30.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, U.S. regulatory steps on digital-asset rules, and Ripple product news.

crypto.name: Solana
crypto.move: Down 0.4% in 24h, up 1.4% this week, to about $105 (down 10% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Solana moved roughly in line with the market as its Alpenglow upgrade, a major overhaul aimed at much faster transaction finality, was set to go live on Wednesday. Big upgrades can attract buyers but also carry execution risk.
crypto.meaning: A smooth Alpenglow launch would be a meaningful technical milestone, but price has lagged this month. Watch for any network problems in the first days after launch.

outlook.bullCase: A trouble-free upgrade and stronger crypto risk appetite could lift SOL back toward $115–$120.
outlook.bearCase: Any outage or bug after the upgrade, or a bitcoin drop below $82,500, could push SOL under $100.
outlook.watch: Network stability after Alpenglow, bitcoin's $82,500–$84,000 zone, and Solana ETF flows.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Up 0.58% to 7,757 at Wednesday's close, about 1% below its record near 7,845; futures are down about 0.4% in evening trading
stocks.why: Stocks rose as SpaceX's strong quarter revived enthusiasm for AI-related tech, Super Micro raised its sales forecast sharply and cybersecurity stocks jumped 5–7% after a critical software flaw was disclosed. Netflix and AT&T were the big drags. The VIX, Wall Street's 'fear gauge', slipped to about 16.7.
stocks.meaning: The index is near its highs heading into the busiest stretch of earnings season. A 10-year yield above 5.1% still makes stocks look expensive relative to bonds.

outlook.bullCase: A recovery in futures by Thursday's open, solid results from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon next week, and a calm Fed on Oct. 28 could push it to a new record above 7,845.
outlook.bearCase: A hawkish Fed, yields pushing toward 5.3%, or an oil spike above $115 could drag it back toward 7,600.
outlook.watch: The 10-year yield, Brent crude, and megacap earnings reactions.

stocks.why: Tech led: SpaceX jumped after beating forecasts, Tesla rose ahead of its report and on merger talk, chip stocks firmed after Super Micro's outlook, and cybersecurity names rallied. Alphabet's 1.6% slide trimmed the gain.
stocks.meaning: The AI trade is back in favour, but Tesla's after-hours reversal shows how quickly sentiment can turn. The bar for Big Tech results next week is high.

outlook.bullCase: Upbeat AI revenue and spending commentary from Meta, Microsoft and Alphabet could carry it back toward the 27,500–27,700 highs.
outlook.bearCase: Disappointing cloud growth or investors balking at huge AI spending could send it back to about 26,000.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.move: Closed up 0.5% at $697.52, then jumped as much as 6% after hours on earnings; the gain had narrowed to a little over 2% by about 9 p.m. ET
stocks.why: Third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion, beating the roughly $63.3 billion expected, and earnings were $7.40 a share excluding a $9.9 billion legal charge ($3.83 including it). Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $73–$76 billion has a midpoint above consensus, and Meta narrowed 2026 capital spending to $135–$145 billion (raising the low end) while giving no 2027 number yet beyond saying AI investment stays heavy. It also plans to hand out one new non-voting Class C share for every existing share in January 2027, which works like a 2-for-1 split.
stocks.meaning: The core ad business is growing fast, which supports the stock, but AI spending pushed free cash flow negative (about -$2.1 billion) this quarter. A separate $25 billion penalty imposed by a New Mexico judge in a privacy case is under appeal and adds legal uncertainty.

outlook.bullCase: If the after-hours gain holds and analysts lift targets, it could recover toward the $740–$780 range it held earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: Worry about open-ended 2027 spending or more legal costs could fade the gain and send it back below $690.
outlook.watch: Thursday's trading, analyst target changes, and 2027 spending commentary.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.move: Closed up 3.4% at $386.47, then fell more than 3% after hours (roughly $373–$375) after an early gain reversed
stocks.why: Tesla rose during the day on Musk's comments that Tesla and SpaceX formed committees to study a merger. After the close it reported adjusted earnings of $0.48 a share versus about $0.45 expected and revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year ago and slightly below some forecasts; free cash flow of $1.5 billion beat expectations of a cash burn because spending came in about $3 billion lower than expected. Shares first rose about 2%, then turned lower during the call as Tesla cut its 2026 capital-spending plan to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion and Musk said reaching 20,000 Optimus robots a week will take at least a year.
stocks.meaning: The core business is weak: operating income fell 56% to $718 million and deliveries slipped 2%, so the stock still trades mostly on robotaxi, Optimus and SpaceX-merger hopes. Lower spending helps cash flow but can read as a slower AI push, which is what the after-hours selling suggests.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete merger progress or a smooth Cybercab expansion to Dallas next month could bring it back toward $400–$410.
outlook.bearCase: If the after-hours drop holds and analysts trim targets, it could slide toward $355–$365.
outlook.watch: Thursday's open, analyst target changes, merger committee news, and the NHTSA Cybercab response due Oct. 30.

stocks.name: SpaceX
stocks.move: Closed up 7.8% at $159.31, after rising as much as 12% intraday
stocks.why: SpaceX's third-quarter results beat forecasts: revenue was about $14.6 billion versus about $12.7 billion expected, and earnings per share were $0.35 versus $0.14. Its AI business brought in about $7.6 billion, more than Starlink and rockets combined. Elon Musk also said SpaceX and Tesla have set up special committees to study a possible merger. Up to 1.3 billion shares become free to sell on Thursday as a lockup expires.
stocks.meaning: The beat shows how central AI has become to SpaceX's story. A large lockup expiry on Thursday, when up to 1.3 billion early shares can be sold, could add selling pressure even after good news.

outlook.bullCase: If buyers absorb Thursday's unlocked shares and merger talks progress, traders are eyeing resistance around $172.
outlook.bearCase: Heavy selling from newly unlocked holders could push it back below support near $150.
outlook.watch: Thursday's lockup expiry, any merger details, and trading volume.

stocks.name: Lam Research
stocks.move: Fell about 6.8% after hours on its outlook, despite beating forecasts
stocks.why: The chip-equipment maker reported revenue of $8.22 billion, up 54% from a year ago, and adjusted earnings of $2.20 a share, both ahead of forecasts. It guided next-quarter revenue to about $8.6 billion and earnings to about $2.33 a share, which only slightly topped analyst estimates. After a big run on AI chip-factory demand, investors wanted a bigger raise.
stocks.meaning: Lam sells the machines that make memory and AI chips, so its outlook is read as a signal for chip spending. A drop on a beat shows how high expectations are across the semiconductor trade.

outlook.bullCase: Strong spending plans from chipmakers and Big Tech next week could help it recover the after-hours drop.
outlook.bearCase: If the after-hours loss holds and other chip-equipment makers guide cautiously, the selling could spread to the wider chip sector.
outlook.watch: Thursday's open, peers' results (KLA, Applied Materials), and Big Tech capital spending plans.

stocks.name: Strategy
stocks.why: Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder with about 848,000 BTC, tends to move two to three times as much as bitcoin. It rose with bitcoin's bounce above $84,000 and with crypto stocks broadly after the OCC finalized stablecoin rules. A Barclays target raise to $175 and a larger buyback authorization have also supported it.
stocks.meaning: MSTR is effectively a leveraged bet on bitcoin, so it amplifies both gains and losses. Its moves today say more about bitcoin than about the company.

outlook.bullCase: Bitcoin reclaiming $84,000 and moving toward $87,500 could lift MSTR toward the $165 area.
outlook.bearCase: A bitcoin break below $82,400 would likely send MSTR back under $140; with bitcoin back near $82,800, an early pullback Thursday is possible.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin's direction, Strategy's weekly purchase filings, and its Q3 results.

stocks.name: Coinbase
stocks.move: Up 3.6% to $177.08, still down about 21% this year
stocks.why: Coinbase gained after the OCC finalized its GENIUS Act stablecoin rules, which set reserve, redemption and risk standards for issuers. Coinbase shares in revenue from Circle's USDC stablecoin, so a clear federal framework helps, and firmer bitcoin prices support trading activity.
stocks.meaning: Clear rules reduce a long-running uncertainty, but whether exchanges can keep paying rewards on stablecoin balances is still unresolved before the January 2027 start date.

outlook.bullCase: Bitcoin pushing toward $87,000 and favourable guidance on stablecoin rewards could lift it toward $190–$200.
outlook.bearCase: A crypto pullback or restrictive rewards rules could send it back toward $165.
outlook.watch: Bitcoin price, regulators' stance on stablecoin rewards, and Coinbase's earnings date.

calendar.why: Cloud growth and AI spending plans are key for tech stocks and for crypto, which has been tracking the Nasdaq.

calendar.label: U.S. core PCE inflation; Amazon earnings (after the close)
calendar.why: PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; Amazon's AWS growth and holiday outlook matter for tech.

calendar.label: Apple earnings (after the close)
calendar.why: The largest index weight; iPhone and services results move the S&P 500.

calendar.label: Zcash NU7 upgrade (about 7:50 p.m. ET)
calendar.why: Developers scheduled activation for this time; upgrade events often bring sharp ZEC swings.

calendar.label: U.S. October jobs report (8:30 a.m. ET)
calendar.why: A strong report could push yields higher and raise the odds of a Fed hike.

calendar.label: U.S. October CPI inflation (8:30 a.m. ET)
calendar.why: September's CPI ran hot at 3.7%; another hot reading would pressure stocks, bonds and crypto.
